title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

plan.title: Too much of one thing, none of another
Why you hold on the way you do
How you fight, and how you make up
How you show love vs how you need it

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. When you fall, you don't wait for permission. You decide, then inform them.

Bom: It's so flattering to be chosen like that.

Yeon: It's flattering in week one. By week six they'd like a vote.

Let the next one catch up. Ask one question a date that you don't already know the answer to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fall in love. You announce it.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You fall by melting. Their laugh, their texts, the way they said your name once.

Yeon: And then you shape yourself around them before they've even asked for anything.

Bom: Falling soft is lovely. Losing yourself isn't part of the deal.

Keep one thing that's only yours while you fall. A class, a friend night, a Sunday ritual. Protect it like it's a date.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fall softly. Just keep your own floor under you.

strong.text:
With a strong chart behind it, the flirting style above carries an edge of certainty. You flirt like someone who expects it to work, and it usually does. The blind spot is reading a polite laugh as a yes, or pushing a little past the point where the other person was still deciding.

Try leaving space on purpose. Say the charming thing, then let them come toward you. Ask a question and wait for the full answer. Strong charts underestimate how magnetic a pause can be. Being slightly less available for one beat makes everything you do say land harder.

And watch for the competitive streak. Strong charts sometimes flirt to win, to be the most interesting person in the room or to prove they still have it, rather than to connect with the one person in front of them. If you notice you're performing for an audience, turn the volume down and ask them something real. Connection is quieter than victory and much more fun to take home.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One charming line, then a pause. Let them walk the last step.

weak.text:
With a weak chart, the flirting style above has a habit of retreating halfway. You send a signal, then take it back before anyone can react: the compliment followed by a joke, the invitation followed by "no worries if not." It protects you from rejection. It also makes you hard to read.

Try finishing one signal fully this month. Give the compliment and stop talking. Make the invitation with a time and a place. You don't need to be bolder than you are. You just need to stop editing yourself halfway through being charming.

It also helps to remember that flirting is a two-way game. You don't have to carry it. Ask a question and let them be charming back. Weak charts sometimes work so hard at being likable that they never find out whether they actually like the other person. Halfway through the evening, ask yourself: am I enjoying them, or just hoping they enjoy me?

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Finish the compliment. No joke after it, no take-backs.

strong.text:
A strong chart attaches with a firm grip and a strong opinion about how things should go. You're reliable and you expect reliability. When a partner doesn't match your pace or your plan, you can read it as a lack of commitment rather than a difference in style.

Try naming your expectations early and asking theirs, out loud, like two people comparing calendars. "I like to talk every day. What do you like?" It sounds unromantic. It prevents a whole season of quiet resentment, the kind where you keep score and they don't even know there's a game.

When conflict hits, strong charts tend to hold their ground and wait for their partner to come around. That can turn a small disagreement into a long silence. Try being the first to reach back, even when you think you were right. A short "I don't like this distance, can we talk?" isn't losing. It's the move that tells your partner the relationship matters more to you than the scoreboard.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're keeping score. They don't know there's a game. Tell them the rules.

weak.text:
A weak chart attaches through need, which is not a dirty word. You need reassurance, closeness, signs that you're still wanted. The trouble starts when you hide the need until it leaks out sideways: as anxiety, as checking, as testing whether they'll notice you've gone quiet.

Try asking for one specific reassurance directly. "Can you text me when you land?" "Tell me if you're upset, so I don't guess." Small requests made early are easy to meet. Big ones made at midnight after three days of silence are much harder, for both of you.

Watch the habit of shrinking your needs to seem easy to love. It works for a while, and then the needs come back bigger. Partners can't meet what they never saw. The secure version of you isn't someone with no needs. It's someone who says them calmly, early, and trusts the relationship to hold them. You can practice that version with small things first.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for the small reassurance early. It's so much easier than the midnight version.

strong.text:
Strong charts get jealous less often and more forcefully. When it hits, it hits as a challenge: someone is in your territory. You might go cold, compete, or make a point of being fine. None of those say what you actually feel, which is usually a flash of fear about losing something you value.

Try this script: "I felt a bit jealous earlier, and I don't love that I did. Can we talk about it?" It costs your pride about ten seconds. It saves the relationship days of weird energy, and it shows your partner something they rarely get to see: you, slightly unsure.

If you notice jealousy turning into control, checking their phone, setting rules for who they see, stop and look underneath. Control is fear in a suit. Ask what you're afraid of losing, then say that instead. Your partner can reassure a fear. They can only resist a rule.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Admitting jealousy costs you ten seconds of pride. Worth it.

weak.text:
Weak charts feel jealousy as a drop in the floor. Someone else is more interesting, more attractive, easier, and you quietly decide you're about to be replaced. Then you either withdraw or try to become more perfect, neither of which your partner asked for.

When the feeling hits, check the facts before the story. What actually happened? What did your partner actually do? Often the honest answer is "they laughed at someone's joke." Then say the feeling, gently and without accusation. "I felt a bit insecure tonight." Most good partners respond to that sentence with exactly what you need.

It also helps to build your own sources of confidence outside the relationship. A skill you're proud of, friends who adore you, a body you look after. Jealousy thrives where your sense of worth depends on one person's attention. The fuller your own life, the less a stranger at a party can threaten it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Facts first, story second. 'They laughed at a joke' isn't 'I'm being replaced.'

strong.text:
Yeon's extra note for strong charts: your red flag gets louder when you're right. Being correct is not a license to be relentless. If you notice you've made the same point three times, the point isn't the problem anymore, the repetition is.

Pick one fight a month to lose on purpose. Something small, the restaurant, the route, the movie. Notice how it feels to let your partner be right about a thing that doesn't matter. Strong lovers who can lose gracefully are rare, and they are very, very easy to stay with.

One practical habit: after any argument, ask your partner "Was there something you wanted to say that you didn't?" Strong charts often win the conversation and lose the information. That one question brings back what got steamrolled, and it shows that you'd rather understand them than be right.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Lose one small argument a month. On purpose. You'll survive it.

weak.text:
Yeon's extra note for weak charts: your red flag hides behind being nice. Saying yes when you mean no, hinting instead of asking, going along and then quietly resenting it. To your partner it looks like everything is fine, until it suddenly isn't, and they have no idea what happened.

Try one honest no a week. Small ones count. "I don't feel like that restaurant." "I'd rather stay in tonight." Every small no you say out loud makes the big yes more believable. Partners trust people who can disagree with them.

One practical habit: when you feel resentment building, write down the moment it started. Usually it's a yes you didn't mean. Next time that same moment comes up, you'll recognize it, and you can try the honest answer instead. Resentment is just a no that missed its chance.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your 'I'm fine' has a body count. Start disagreeing about restaurants.

strong.text:
One more thing a strong chart needs, and rarely lists: someone who can stand up to you, warmly. Not a rival and not a pushover. A person who says "I see it differently" and doesn't fold when you push back. You'll find it annoying for about a week and then realize it's the first time you've felt truly met.

If your past partners mostly agreed with you, notice that pattern. Agreement feels good. Someone with a backbone of their own feels like home.

When you date, test for this early. Disagree with them about something small and watch what they do. Do they fold, fight, or stay curious? The curious ones are your people. They'll keep you honest without making it a war, and they won't be flattened by your certainty.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You need someone who disagrees with you kindly. It'll feel like home.

weak.text:
One more thing a weak chart needs, and rarely lists: someone whose care is consistent rather than dramatic. Big gestures followed by long silences will keep you anxious however romantic they look. What steadies you is the ordinary stuff, the daily text, the plan that happens, the person who is the same on Tuesday as on Saturday.

If you've been drawn to intensity, notice that pull. Intensity feels like love to a chart looking for proof. Consistency is what love feels like once you stop needing proof.

When you date, test for this early. Notice who replies when they said they would, who makes the second plan, who remembers what you told them last time. Those boring signals predict more about your happiness than any chemistry on the first night. Let consistency be attractive to you. It is the most underrated trait in love.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Intensity feels like love. Consistency is what love actually feels like.

peer_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls it the peer family: siblings, friends, rivals. In love it gives you a strong sense of self and a fierce need to stay equal. You want a partner, not a parent and not a project, and you can turn competitive when you feel outranked, even over small things like who's busier or who sacrificed more. The gift is that you never disappear into a relationship. The work is letting closeness feel like teamwork rather than a tie you're trying to break. Partners do best with you when they have their own full lives. Look for that from the start.

A good test for a new partner: do they have plans that don't include you, and are you glad about it? If yes, the peer energy has room to be friendship instead of rivalry, and that is where it shines.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. You want an equal. Just don't race them to the car.

output_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the output family: charm, creativity, expression, the way you make people feel. With a strong Day Master behind it you are a gifted lover in the playful sense: you flirt well, you make dates memorable, you say things people remember for years. Output also resists rules, so you may chafe at the parts of love that are routine. The trick is to bring that creativity into ordinary days rather than saving it for the beginning. A clever note on a Tuesday counts more than a grand gesture in month one.

Watch, too, for the moment your playfulness becomes a way to avoid a serious talk. A joke at the right time is charm. A joke every time the conversation gets real is a door you keep closing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your {heavy_el} makes love feel like an adventure. Bring some of it to Tuesdays.

wealth_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. That's the wealth family: what you pursue and take care of. In love it makes you a provider and a planner. You show affection by making life work for the person you love: arrangements, practical help, a future with dates on it. A strong chart can carry this well. The shadow is treating love as something to secure rather than something to share, and feeling unappreciated when your efforts aren't noticed. Say what the effort means. "I booked this because I wanted time with you" lands much better than a silent spreadsheet of good deeds.

It also helps to let your partner plan something now and then, even if they do it less efficiently. Being planned for is a form of love you rarely get to feel, and you deserve to feel it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You show love with logistics. Say why, or it just looks like admin.

power_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. That's the power family: duty, standards, how things should be done. A strong chart wears it as integrity. You're loyal, you mean your promises, and you have a clear picture of what a good relationship looks like. You may also hold partners to that picture a bit tightly. Rules are useful in love when both people wrote them. Check that yours were agreed, not just assumed, and leave some room for the parts of a person that don't fit any template.

When a partner falls short of your picture, ask before you judge: was this a broken promise, or a promise I made for them in my head? Most of the hurt lives in the second kind.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your standards keep love safe. Just check your partner signed off on them.

resource_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. That's the resource family: comfort, learning, inner life. You're self-contained and thoughtful in love, comfortable with silence, good at understanding a partner deeply. The risk is staying in the understanding and not moving into action. You know exactly what they need and wait for the perfect moment to give it. Act sooner. Thoughtfulness becomes love when it turns into something the other person can actually see: a plan, a touch, a sentence said out loud.

A small rule helps: when you catch yourself thinking a lovely thought about them, act on it within a day. Send it, say it, do it. Kept inside, it's only a thought. Shared, it becomes part of the relationship.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You understand them perfectly. Now do something they can actually see.

output_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the output family: giving, expressing, performing. On a weak chart it drains you. You're the generous lover who plans the surprise, writes the long message and remembers everything, and then wonders why you feel tired and slightly unseen. The fix isn't giving less love. It's letting love come in. Notice when someone does something for you and receive it without immediately returning the favor. Practice the plain words "thank you" with nothing added.

Look for partners who give without being asked, and notice how uncomfortable that feels at first. The discomfort is just unfamiliarity. Give it a few weeks and it starts to feel like rest.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Practice receiving. 'Thank you' with nothing added. That's it.

wealth_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. That's the wealth family: what you reach for and try to hold. Classical readers call this pattern wealth heavy, self light: a lot to manage with little backup. In love it can look like being drawn to partners who need looking after, or taking responsibility for the whole relationship's mood and future. You end up holding the steering wheel and the map while running on fumes. Pick partners who take turns driving, and let them.

Notice, too, if you're attracted to people who are going through a crisis. Rescuing feels meaningful to a chart like yours. A relationship works better when both people can stand, and you deserve someone who sometimes rescues you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You keep dating people you have to carry. Pick someone who takes turns driving.

power_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. That's the power family: pressure, rules, judgment. On a weak chart it shows up as a nervous carefulness in love. You try hard to be a good partner, you notice every sign of disapproval, and criticism lands like a verdict. You may be drawn to strong, decisive people who feel safe and then feel smaller around them. Look for warmth before strength. The right partner makes you feel more relaxed, not more on your best behavior.

When a partner criticizes you, try separating the feedback from the verdict. "You forgot the reservation" is feedback. "You're careless" is a verdict you added yourself. Answer the first, and drop the second.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pick warmth over strength. The right person relaxes you.

rooted_on_paper.text:
In love, that split can look like confidence on the outside and uncertainty underneath. You can seem like the steady one, sure of what you want, and still feel a sudden wobble when a partner goes quiet. Neither feeling is fake. One is the plenty you can see, the other is the root you're missing. Choose partners who are consistent, and tell them early that reassurance matters to you. People who love you will give it gladly.

It also helps to stop testing whether they'll stay. Weak charts with plenty on paper sometimes act casual to see if the other person cares enough to chase. Skip the test and ask for what you want instead.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Steady outside, wobbly inside. Both are you. Pick consistent people.

output_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, how love gets expressed. A strong chart without output tends to love in actions and silence. You'd fight for your partner and still struggle to tell them you missed them. Borrow some output: a sentence a day that names what you feel, a note, a voice message. Your partner shouldn't have to infer your love from the fact that you fixed their bike. Start small. One sentence before bed, one note in their bag. Expression gets easier with reps, like anything else you've trained.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You fixed their bike. Lovely. Now use your words.

wealth_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, pursuit. You have strength without a strong instinct to chase, so you may wait to be approached, or let promising connections drift because you didn't push. If you want someone, borrow a little wealth energy. Make the plan, name the date, follow up. Being chosen is nice. Choosing is nicer. Waiting can look like being relaxed. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's just losing people you liked to someone who asked first.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Being chosen is nice. Choosing someone is even better. Make the plan.

power_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, the structure. A strong chart without structure loves freely and sometimes carelessly: forgetting the anniversary, changing plans, assuming the bond is obvious. Borrow some structure. A standing date night, a habit of checking in, keeping the small promises. Commitment isn't a cage for you. It's the thing that lets your partner relax. Structure isn't the enemy of passion. It's what lets your partner trust the passion will still be there next Thursday.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Standing date night. Calendar it. Your charm needs a schedule.

resource_strong.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, nurture. You're strong without being cushioned, so you may not know how to be looked after. When a partner tries to take care of you, you deflect, joke or say you're fine. Let them. Receiving care is a skill and a gift to the person giving it. Strong people who can lean a little are much easier to love. You might notice you're drawn to people who need you more than they look after you. That's the missing element talking. Choose some care for yourself, too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: When they try to look after you, let them. It's a gift both ways.

output_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element, expression. That keeps a weak chart from pouring itself out too fast, which is protective. It also means your feelings can stay invisible. Partners may think you're cooler than you are. Show love in small, sustainable ways: a message when you think of them, a hand on their arm, one honest sentence on a quiet evening. Your partner will learn your quieter language if you teach them a few words of it. Tell them what your small signs mean.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A tiny sign of love still counts. You don't need a speech.

wealth_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, the urge to pursue. On a weak chart that can be a relief: you don't chase people who don't want you. The risk is waiting so long for certainty that the moment passes. Practice tiny moves. Suggest the coffee. Send the first message. Low stakes, real practice. Every small move you make teaches your nervous system that reaching for something you want is survivable. It is, and it gets easier.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Certainty never arrives first. Suggest the coffee anyway.

power_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element, outside pressure. For a weak chart that's mostly good: fewer rules weighing on you. But it can also mean you're unsure what's reasonable to expect from a partner. It's reasonable to expect respect, consistency and kindness. Write down three expectations and keep them nearby. They'll help you recognize the right person faster. Expectations aren't demands. They are how you recognize respect when it shows up, and how you notice when it doesn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Respect, consistency, kindness. Reasonable to expect. Write them down.

resource_weak.text: {miss_el} is missing from your visible chart, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, nurture. That's part of why you may look for comfort in partners, sometimes before you know them well. Comfort is a fair thing to want. Just build a few sources: friends, family, rest, things that soothe you. When love is one source of comfort among several, you choose partners for who they are rather than for how much you need them. And when love does come, let it be one good thing in a life full of good things, not the whole meal.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Build comfort from many places. Then you can choose love freely.

none_strong.text: Every element turns up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only as hidden stems. In love that gives you range: you can be playful, steady, passionate, practical or tender. A strong chart can switch modes so fast that partners don't know which you they'll get. Let them in on it. "I'm in fix-it mode tonight" or "I just need to be held" tells them which version is showing up. Your range is a gift. It just works best with a little narration, so the people close to you can keep up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tell them which you is showing up tonight. Saves everyone a guess.

none_weak.text: Every element turns up somewhere in your pillars, even if some only as hidden stems. In love that means you have many ways to give and receive affection, even if you don't always have the energy for them. Choose the one the moment needs. Some days that's a joke, some days a long hug, some days an early night. You don't need to be everything at once to be a wonderful partner. On low days, choose the gentlest tool. On good days, try the one you use least. That's how range grows into confidence.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pick the one kind thing today needs. That's plenty.

resource.title: What steadies you in love: {helper_el}
resource.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. For your weak {dm_el} chart it's {helper_el}, the one that nourishes your Day Master. In love, this is the difference between loving from a full cup and loving from an empty one. With enough {helper_el} in your life, you choose partners more freely, you ask for what you need with less fear, and you stop mistaking relief for chemistry. A simple check before any big relationship decision: have I slept, eaten and talked to someone who loves me this week? If not, refuel first and decide second.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Love from a full cup. Yours fills with {helper_el}.

peer.title: What steadies you in love: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours already carries plenty of nourishment on paper, so the best support is your own element, {helper_el}. In love that means equality and friendship. You do best with a partner who is also your friend, and with friends who are honest about your relationships. Peers keep you grounded in a way advice never quite does. A simple check before any big relationship decision: what would my most honest friend say? Then actually ask them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your element is {helper_el}. Date your friend, keep your friends close.

output.title: What balances you in love: {helper_el}
output.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and for you that's {helper_el}, the element your Day Master produces. In love that means expression, play and generosity. You're happiest when the energy flows out as affection, creativity and fun rather than turning into control or impatience. Use it. Make things for the people you love. A simple check when a relationship feels tense: where has my energy been going lately? If it's been stuck inside you, find it a creative outlet before it turns into control.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. Spend your energy on play, not control.

wealth.title: What balances you in love: {helper_el}
wealth.text: Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours is strong and already expressive, so what balances you is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master shapes and cares for. In love that means building something concrete together: a home, a ritual, a shared project. You thrive when affection becomes something you can both point to. A simple check when a relationship feels vague: what are we actually building together right now? If the answer is nothing, start something small and shared.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your balancing element is {helper_el}. Build a shared ritual, then keep it.

wood.text: In a relationship, {helper_el} looks like growing together. Walks, classes, plans for the future, a partner who encourages your ambitions and lets you encourage theirs. If things feel stuck between you, plan something that grows: a garden, a savings goal for a trip, a skill you both learn badly together.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood in love: growing side by side. Take a class together.

fire.text: In a relationship, {helper_el} looks like warmth that shows. Laughter, affection in public, dinners with friends, saying "I love you" without waiting for the perfect moment. If things feel cold between you, add warmth on purpose: a weekend with friends, a candlelit dinner, more touch, more laughter, more saying it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire in love: warmth that shows. Say it out loud.

earth.text: In a relationship, {helper_el} looks like steadiness. Shared routines, a home that feels calm, someone who does what they said they'd do. If things feel shaky between you, add structure: a weekly ritual, a shared calendar, a Sunday dinner you never skip.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth in love: routines, a calm home, promises kept.

metal.text: In a relationship, {helper_el} looks like clarity. Honest conversations, clear agreements, boundaries both of you respect, a partner who means what they say. If things feel blurry between you, add clarity: a calm talk about what each of you expects, and a decision you both stick to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal in love: clear agreements. Romantic? Surprisingly, yes.

water.text: In a relationship, {helper_el} looks like depth and rest. Long talks, quiet evenings, space for both of you to recharge without anyone taking it personally. If things feel tense between you, add rest: early nights, slow mornings, an evening each where nobody needs anything.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water in love: depth, rest, space that nobody takes personally.

rat.text: Saju calls the branch under your Day Master the spouse palace: the seat of your partner and the you that only a partner sees. Yours is the Rat, 子, midwinter Water and one of the four peach-blossom branches. Classical readers link peach blossom with natural charm, and the Rat's version is quick wit and late-night intimacy. Up close you're more emotional than your public self, private about it, and deeply loyal once you trust. You need a partner who's curious about your mind and patient with your guardedness. Give them a key early. The Rat's burrow is lovely inside, and most people never get invited in. Peach-blossom spouse palaces attract easily, so interest is rarely your problem. Choosing well is. Let attraction be the start of your judgment, not the end of it, and give the people who are kind on an ordinary Tuesday as much credit as the ones who dazzle on a Saturday.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat spouse palace: witty, private, loyal. Hand someone a key early.

ox.text: Saju calls the branch under your Day Master the spouse palace: the seat of your partner and the you that only a partner sees. Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth that stores Metal. Up close you're steady, devoted and slow to open, but once you do, you're in for the long haul. You show love by showing up, year after year. Your challenge is flexibility. The Ox can be stubborn about how things are done at home. Pick the hills worth standing on, and let the rest be your partner's way sometimes. Storehouse branches keep a lot inside: hopes, hurts, memories, plans. Classical readers link them with a private, reflective streak. Let a partner into the storehouse a room at a time. They can't love the parts of you they've never been shown.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox spouse palace: devoted and stubborn. Let them load the dishwasher wrong.

tiger.text: Saju calls the branch under your Day Master the spouse palace: the seat of your partner and the you that only a partner sees. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood carrying Fire, and one of the travel branches. Up close you're bold, protective and restless. You need a partner who's an adventure, not a fence. You'll defend the people you love fiercely and you hate feeling managed. The trick is letting closeness and freedom coexist: shared adventures, separate ones too, and a home base you both enjoy returning to. Travel branches, the ones classical readers call yeokma, need movement in love: trips, change, shared growth. A relationship that stands still too long will start to feel like a cage even when it's kind. Build adventure into it on purpose, and it will hold you happily.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger spouse palace: you need adventures together, and some apart.

rabbit.text: Saju calls the branch under your Day Master the spouse palace: the seat of your partner and the you that only a partner sees. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood and one of the four peach-blossom branches. Up close you're gentle, romantic and attentive to beauty, the partner who remembers what was playing on your first date. You avoid conflict to keep things soft, which can let small hurts pile up. Practice the gentle complaint, said early. Softness and honesty can live in the same sentence. Peach-blossom spouse palaces attract easily, so interest is rarely your problem. Choosing well is. Let attraction be the start of your judgment, not the end of it, and give the people who are kind on an ordinary Tuesday as much credit as the ones who dazzle on a Saturday.

panel.speaker: yeon

fast.speaker: yeon
fast.text: Fast and hard, you said. So you've named the kids by date three. Let's check the brakes.

slow.speaker: bom
slow.text: Slowly, then all at once. The prettiest way to fall, and the scariest one.

overthink.speaker: yeon
overthink.text: "I don't fall, I overthink." You do fall. You just do it in your head first, for months, alone.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You didn't say how you fall. That's fine. Your birthday already told on you.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

mu-earth.how-you-fall:
You fall like a season changes. Slowly, then one day it's just different. You feel it long before you show it.

Bom: You need to trust before you can love. That's wise.

Yeon: It's wise. It also means some people give up waiting while you're still running background checks.

Bom: Show a little before you're sure. A hint. A "I liked tonight". It helps.
mu-earth.flirting: You flirt by being useful, and you may not even call it flirting. Carrying their bags, making sure they got home, showing up with snacks because they mentioned they skipped lunch. It's steady, practical care, and the people who notice it melt. The people who don't might wonder if you're interested at all, because you rarely say the soft thing out loud. Your humor helps a lot here. Dry, understated jokes are your secret weapon, and when you let them out, people get a glimpse of the warm landscape behind the cliff face. Try one small step past comfort: tell them you like them, plainly. You don't need poetry. "I like spending time with you" from a mountain sounds like a whole sonnet.
mu-earth.attachment: Your pattern looks secure and sometimes leans avoidant. You're reliable and calm, the opposite of dramatic, and you rarely panic about where a relationship stands. But emotional conversations can make you go quiet and still, like a hill waiting out a storm. You'd rather fix a problem than talk about how it feels, and when a partner wants to process, you might reach for solutions or simply shut down until it passes. That's not coldness. It's how you protect a very big, very loyal heart. Your growth edge is staying present in the feelings part. Sit in the conversation without fixing it. Say "that sounds hard" and mean it. You'll be surprised how much closer people feel when the mountain just listens.
mu-earth.jealousy: You rarely get jealous, and when you do, it looks like nothing. That's the problem. You don't sulk or accuse. You just become a little more distant, a little more silent, and quietly start reconsidering how much you trust this person. Your trigger is inconsistency. If someone says one thing and does another, flirts openly when they promised they wouldn't, or hides something small, your entire internal foundation shifts. You don't care much about rivals. You care about reliability. Because you don't express it, the other person might not realize there's anything wrong until you've already half withdrawn. Say it while it's still small. "I noticed this and it bothered me." Mountains erode slowly. It's better to repair one crack than rebuild the whole slope.
mu-earth.red-flag: Yeon's take: you're stubborn to the point of geology. Once you've decided how something should go, you stop listening, and your partner feels like they're arguing with a wall. A very kind, very supportive wall, but a wall. Second flag: you mistake stability for romance. You can stay comfortable in a relationship that stopped growing years ago because it's familiar and safe. "Nothing's wrong" is not the same as "this is good." Third: you shut down instead of fighting. The silent treatment isn't punishment for you, it's processing, but to your partner it feels like being frozen out. You're allowed to need time. Just say "I need an hour, then let's talk" instead of disappearing into rock.
mu-earth.what-you-need: You need trust, and you need it earned. A partner who is consistent, keeps small promises, and doesn't play games, because you have zero patience for mind tricks. You need someone who appreciates quiet loyalty and doesn't need constant performance of affection to feel loved. Gentle encouragement helps you too: someone who invites you to try new things without pushing, who brings a little color and spontaneity to your steady life. And you need someone who understands that your love shows up as action. When you cook for them or sort out their car, that's a declaration. The best person for you feels like a clear day on a mountain. Calm, open, and worth staying for.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: You love like a mountain. Solid, safe, there for decades.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Your crush timeline runs on geological time.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: You fall slowly. When you finally do, you don't fall back out.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: And when they want to talk about feelings, you suggest fixing the shelf.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Try saying "I like you" out loud. From you it sounds like poetry.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Comfortable is not the same as happy. Check which one you're in.

spring.intro: A mountain in spring, with trees pushing through it from every side. Life tested you early. That's why you're so steady now, and also why "relax" sounds to you like a trick.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You became the calm one because someone had to.

summer.intro: A summer mountain, warmed all the way through. Solid, generous, the one everyone leans on. You give off safety without trying. People tell you things they've never told anyone, and you never repeat them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: People feel safe with you within five minutes. Rare.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain, showing its stone. You turn your weight into output: work done, things built, problems quietly solved. You don't talk about feelings much. You show them by fixing the shelf.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Love language: unasked-for repairs. Every time.

winter.intro: A mountain in winter, holding back the river. You manage things: money, plans, other people's chaos. Very good at it. The cost is that you rarely let anything thaw, including you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not cold. You're frozen on purpose. Different.

earth.intro: A mountain born in Earth's own weeks. Triple solid. You don't move unless you want to, and you almost never want to. Your loyalty is legendary. So is the time it takes you to change your mind.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Persuading you is a geological process.

mu-earth.strong: A strong Mu Earth is a mountain that does not move for anyone. With plenty of support in your chart, you are steady, protective and very sure of what is sensible. In love you give enormous security, but you can also become immovable. Your blind spot is overpowering through stubbornness: refusing new plans, settling arguments by simply not budging, assuming your partner will adjust. They usually do, until one day they stop. Practice saying 'let's try it your way' and actually meaning it. A mountain that lets a path through is still a mountain. It is just easier to love.
mu-earth.weak: A weak Mu Earth is a hill being leaned on from every side. With little support, you still want to be the reliable one, so you carry partners through crises you cannot really afford. You may become the emergency contact, the fixer, the person who never needs anything. Your blind spot is over-giving until you feel empty and heavy at once. Then you go quiet and nobody knows why. Ask for help before you reach that point. Let your partner be the solid ground for a week. Being held is not weakness. It is what lets mountains stay standing.

love-language.text:
Your love language is being there, Mu. Reliably, solidly, every time. You're the one who drives across town when the car breaks, who remembers to check the tire pressure, who stays calm in a crisis. Your affection is a mountain they can lean against.

What you need back is trust and loyalty, plainly given. A partner who keeps their word, who doesn't make you guess, who sees your steadiness as love and not as boredom. You also need, though you'll rarely ask, small gestures of care aimed at you: a cup of tea brought to you, a hand on your shoulder after a long day.

The swap that helps: say one feeling a day out loud. "I liked today." "I missed you." Your actions speak loudly, but partners still like to hear the words. A mountain with a voice is a rare and lovely thing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You love by showing up, every single time, Mu. That's rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: 'I liked today.' Three words, Mu. Even mountains can manage that.

good-week.heading: A good week together, for you
good-week.text: A good week for Mu in love: plans kept, no last-minute chaos, a meal cooked together, one outdoor activity, and one moment where your partner looked after you for a change. Predictable sounds dull on paper. For you it's the foundation that lets the fun happen. If the week was chaotic, don't just absorb it. Say so, and ask what you can both change.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your good week: plans kept, a meal made together, something outdoors.

the-fight.text:
Your fighting style is the mountain's, Mu: you don't. Mostly you go quiet and immovable, waiting for the storm to pass. Your partner experiences that as a wall, and walls make people shout louder. When you finally do get angry, it's rare and seismic, and everyone remembers it. You make up by acting normal, which works for you and can feel to them like the issue was never addressed.

Try saying what you feel during the fight, briefly. "I'm frustrated, and I need a minute to think." That turns your stillness from a wall into a pause. And when you make up, name the thing. "I'm sorry I shut down. I was hurt about the weekend." Two sentences, and suddenly they're dealing with a person, not a landscape.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, going silent isn't staying calm. To them it's a wall.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 'I need a minute' turns the wall into a pause. Try it.

mu-earth.title: You took eleven months to say you liked them. They'd moved cities.
mu-earth.text:
You don't rush love. You observe. You test. You wait to be sure. By the time you're sure, you're sure forever.

Bom: Your love is the safest thing a person can have.

Yeon: Your love is also on a delivery schedule of six to eight business months.
mu-earth.end: Yeon: How you fall is slow. Why you fall slow is the interesting part. Next page.

cliff.mu-earth: Yeon: Your flirting style, Mountain: you think you're being | obvious. You are not. You've been "flirting" for a month and they think you're just polite.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Red flag: you call it being steady. Sometimes it's just being unwilling to say what you want.
